NDT training in Pasadena: how it works for Pasadena employers and technicians

Short answer: NDT training for Pasadena, Texas employers and technicians is delivered by Atlantis NDT live online or onsite at your shop, plant or yard, under ASNT Level III oversight, to ASNT SNT-TC-1A. Level I, II and III courses cover UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, with Level III exam preparation. Your employer certifies you under its written practice after training, documented experience, Level III-administered exams and a vision test. Atlantis has no classroom in Pasadena. We bring the training to your crew.

Pasadena sits on the south bank of the Houston Ship Channel, in one of the densest concentrations of refining, chemical and terminal assets in the world. Its industrial district runs along the Ship Channel and State Highway 225, with the Bayport industrial complex and Port Houston's Bayport container terminal to the southeast. Refineries, chemical plants, bulk liquid terminals, fabrication shops and inspection contractors are packed into a few miles. For NDT technicians that means steady plant work year-round, with spring and fall turnaround seasons that can double demand almost overnight.

Pasadena also has a place in the history of mechanical integrity. The 1989 explosion at the Phillips chemical complex in Pasadena was one of the incidents behind OSHA's Process Safety Management standard (29 CFR 1910.119). That standard's mechanical-integrity element still requires covered facilities to inspect and test process equipment according to recognised and generally accepted good engineering practices, using trained personnel. Much of the NDT work along the Ship Channel traces back to that requirement.

This section goes beyond the overview above. It covers per-method course content for Ship Channel work, the SNT-TC-1A path, delivery around turnarounds, Texas radiography requirements, and what Pasadena NDT companies need from a written practice and a Level III. Request a Pasadena training quote whenever you're ready.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Pasadena

All courses follow ASNT SNT-TC-1A and can be delivered to Pasadena candidates as live online theory, onsite theory and practical at the employer's facility, or a blend. Your employer's written practice sets the required hours. Our training-requirements matrix lists the reference figures.

MethodLevelsWhat Pasadena employers use it forPrerequisite
UT (ultrasonic testing)I, II, IIIThickness monitoring on piping circuits and vessels, shear-wave weld examination, and tank shell and floor surveysLevel I: written-practice education and training. Level II: Level I plus documented UT experience
PAUT (phased array UT)II, IIIEncoded weld inspection in lieu of RT on new construction and repairs, corrosion mapping, and inspection for damage mechanisms that need advanced UTUT Level II normally expected
TOFD (time-of-flight diffraction)II, IIIFlaw sizing on thick-wall vessel and heavy piping welds, and as part of advanced UT screening programmesUT Level II normally expected
RT (radiographic testing)I, II, IIIWeld radiography on process piping and vessels, and profile radiography for corrosion under insulationTexas radiographer certification and radiation-safety training in addition to method training
MT (magnetic particle testing)I, IICrack detection on carbon-steel welds, vessel nozzles, structural steel and lifting equipment, including wet fluorescent MT for crackingLevel I: written-practice education and training. Level II: Level I plus MT experience
PT (liquid penetrant testing)I, IISurface examination of stainless and alloy piping, weld overlays and non-magnetic componentsLevel I: written-practice education and training. Level II: Level I plus PT experience
VT (visual testing)I, IIWeld and fit-up visual inspection, external condition surveys of piping, vessels and tanks, and turnaround internal inspectionsLevel I: written-practice education and training. Level II: Level I plus VT experience
ET (eddy current testing)I, IIHeat exchanger and condenser tubing inspection during turnarounds, and surface-crack detection through coatingsLevel I: written-practice education and training. Level II: Level I plus ET experience

UT for Ship Channel plants. The ultrasonic courses cover calibration, straight-beam thickness measurement, angle-beam weld inspection, and indication evaluation. Pasadena candidates focus on thickness-monitoring location practice, high-temperature measurement considerations, and the discipline of recording data so it trends correctly in an owner's inspection database. A Level II who records a thickness reading at the wrong location creates a false corrosion rate.

PAUT and TOFD. Advanced UT is the differentiator between Ship Channel contractors. The phased array course covers focal laws, sectorial and linear scans, encoded scanning, corrosion mapping and data analysis. The TOFD course covers diffraction-based sizing and its limits. Owners increasingly specify advanced UT for weld inspection instead of radiography on repairs and new work, and for screening damage mechanisms such as high-temperature hydrogen attack, where industry practice (API RP 941 as context) calls for advanced ultrasonic techniques. Both courses build on UT Level II.

RT. The radiography course covers sources, exposure calculations, image quality indicators, film and digital interpretation of welds, and the principles of profile radiography for corrosion under insulation.

MT and PT. The magnetic particle course covers magnetisation techniques, wet fluorescent inspection and interpretation of cracking in ferritic steels. The penetrant course covers the full process on stainless and alloy systems, with attention to contaminant control and surface preparation.

ET. The eddy current course covers tubing inspection with bobbin probes, impedance-plane analysis, calibration standards and defect characterisation. Exchanger bundles are a major item on every Pasadena turnaround scope.

VT. The visual course covers direct and remote visual technique, lighting, measurement and documentation for welds, piping, vessel internals and tanks.

Level III. Pasadena companies building an in-house certification programme can prepare a senior technician through ASNT Level III training, with readiness checks via UT Level II practice questions and the PAUT Level II mock exam.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Pasadena, step by step

SNT-TC-1A is employer-based. Your employer issues your certification under its written practice. Here's the sequence.

  1. Employer written practice. Education, training, experience, examination, vision and recertification requirements for each method and level.
  2. Formal training. Classroom training in the method and level, online or onsite, with hours from the written practice. See the training-requirements matrix.
  3. Documented experience. Supervised on-the-job hours in the method, logged and signed. Turnaround work builds hours fast, but only if someone records them.
  4. General exam. A written test of method principles.
  5. Specific exam. A written test on your employer's procedures and equipment and the codes you work to, typically including ASME Section V techniques and plant owner specifications.
  6. Practical exam. A hands-on exam on real specimens, graded by a Level III or a qualified designee.
  7. Vision examination. Near-vision acuity is checked annually, with colour contrast differentiation as required.
  8. Certification. Your employer certifies you.
  9. Recertification. This happens at the interval your written practice defines.

Some owners also run their own qualification or performance-demonstration programmes for advanced techniques. Those sit on top of SNT-TC-1A certification. For the full framework, see SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Pasadena crews

  • Live online theory. Instructor-led, real-time classes. Useful for technicians on twelve-hour turnaround shifts who can't give up a week to a classroom.
  • Onsite at your facility. Groups are trained and examined at your Pasadena shop or yard on your own equipment and specimens that look like plant work.
  • Blended. Online theory completed between jobs, then a concentrated onsite practical block.

Timing is everything on the Ship Channel. Spring and fall turnaround seasons pull every available technician into the plants. The smart window for training is the weeks before a season, so newly certified technicians arrive ready for the surge, or the quieter weeks after one. Tell us your turnaround calendar and we plan around it. Cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day. Ask about onsite training for your Pasadena crew, or see how online NDT training works.

Where NDT technicians work in Pasadena

Refining. Pasadena's refinery and the others along the Ship Channel run continuous in-service inspection programmes on piping, vessels, exchangers and tanks, with major turnaround scopes on a regular cycle. API inspection codes guide in-service programmes, and ASME B31.3 and Section VIII govern new construction and repairs.

Chemicals and the Bayport complex. Chemical and polymer plants along the channel and in the Bayport industrial complex handle a wide range of process fluids and damage mechanisms, creating demand for UT thickness monitoring, advanced UT, PT on alloy systems, and ET on exchangers.

Terminals and storage. Bulk liquid terminals and tank farms along the channel need tank inspection (API 650 for construction and API 653 for in-service work are the usual references), thickness surveys, floor scanning and weld inspection. Dock lines and loading-arm piping add further scope.

Port and marine. Port Houston's Bayport terminal and the ship-channel waterfront create work on cranes, structural steel and marine structures, typically under AWS D1.1 and customer requirements.

Fabrication and repair shops. Pasadena's fabrication yards and machine shops build and repair piping spools, vessels, skids and structural modules. They need certified VT, MT, PT, UT and RT personnel for their own quality control.

Pipelines. Product and gas pipelines serving Ship Channel facilities need weld inspection during construction and repair, with API 1104 as the usual reference. The Railroad Commission of Texas oversees intrastate pipeline safety alongside federal rules.

Site access requirements. Many Ship Channel facilities are regulated under the Maritime Transportation Security Act, so unescorted access often requires a TWIC card. Most plants also require a contractor safety orientation before a technician can badge in. These are site requirements, not NDT certifications, but employers expect new hires to have them or to get them quickly.

Radiography licensing in Texas. Texas is an NRC Agreement State. Industrial radiography is licensed by the Texas Department of State Health Services (DSHS) Radiation Control Program. Texas requires individual radiographers to hold state radiographer certification and carry their identification on the job, in addition to the employer's licence, operating and emergency procedures, and radiation-safety training. Ship Channel RT is often performed at night or behind barricades to keep other crafts clear of the controlled area, which makes safety discipline a core part of the job. Atlantis teaches the RT method. Licensing and radiation safety remain the employer's responsibility.

What Pasadena employers typically ask for. SNT-TC-1A Level II in UT (often with PAUT), plus MT, PT and VT, and a clean certification file. Owners and contractors also ask for a TWIC card, safety orientations and turnaround experience. Some plant roles ask for API individual inspector certifications or AWS CWI. Those are separate schemes with their own certifying bodies, and Atlantis trains to SNT-TC-1A only.

Level III services and written practices for Pasadena NDT companies

Ship Channel plant owners audit their NDT contractors hard, and the findings are predictable. The written practice doesn't cover the advanced techniques the company actually performs. Experience logs are incomplete. Practical exams have no retained checklists. Procedures aren't approved by the designated Level III. Any one of these can cost a contractor a spot on an approved-vendor list.

Atlantis helps Pasadena employers with:

  • Written-practice development and review. SNT-TC-1A written practices that cover your real methods and techniques, including PAUT and TOFD, and that line up with owner specifications.
  • Outsourced Level III services. Examinations, procedure review and approval, and certification file audits before an owner audit.
  • Corporate programmes. Multi-method, multi-level training plans that build turnaround-ready crews.
  • SNT-TC-1A guidance. Clear interpretation of the recommended practice for your scope.

Book a Level III consultation for your Pasadena company.

Practise before the practical exam

The Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees rehearse 12 NDT methods in five environments, including an oil and gas site, a storage tank, a welding workshop, an NDT lab and an aircraft hangar. Pasadena trainees can walk through plant and tank inspection technique before touching real equipment.

It is practice only. The simulator does not replace hands-on training, and it does not replace the practical exam on real specimens that SNT-TC-1A requires.

Your instructor

Programmes are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He sets course content, oversees practical training and examinations, and leads written-practice and Level III work for Atlantis clients. Pasadena employers work directly with a Level III.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Pasadena

How do I get NDT certified in Pasadena, Texas?

Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, you complete formal training in a method, build documented on-the-job experience, pass general, specific and practical exams administered under a Level III, and pass a vision test. Your employer then certifies you under its written practice. Atlantis delivers the training online or onsite.

Can I take NDT training online in Texas?

Yes, for theory. Atlantis runs live online classes for Level I, II and III theory in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET. The practical training and practical exam must be done in person on real specimens. See online NDT training.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

Your employer's written practice sets the classroom hours and documented experience for Level I and Level II. Experience usually takes longest. See the reference figures in our training-requirements matrix.

Do I need a license for radiography in Texas?

Yes. The employer needs a licence from the Texas DSHS Radiation Control Program, and individual radiographers must hold Texas radiographer certification and carry their identification while working. SNT-TC-1A RT method certification is separate.

What does NDT training cost in Pasadena?

We don't publish prices. Quotes depend on method, level, group size, online or onsite delivery, and any written-practice or Level III support. You'll receive a cohort or onsite quote within one business day. Request a Pasadena training quote.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Pasadena employers?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A is the standard framework for NDT personnel along the Houston Ship Channel. Because certification is employer-based, each new employer certifies you under its own written practice, using your training and experience records.

Do I need a TWIC card to work in NDT in Pasadena?

For many Ship Channel facilities regulated under the Maritime Transportation Security Act, yes, for unescorted access. Plants also require their own safety orientations. Neither replaces NDT certification, but employers expect both.

Which NDT method should I learn first for Ship Channel work?

UT thickness and VT are the most common entry points, followed by MT and PT. Technicians who add PAUT after UT Level II are among the most sought after for plant and turnaround work.

Can Atlantis train our Pasadena crew onsite?

Yes. Onsite delivery at your shop or yard, timed around your turnaround calendar, is the standard model for groups. Ask about onsite training for your Pasadena crew.

Does my certification transfer between Ship Channel contractors?

No. SNT-TC-1A certifications belong to the issuing employer. Your training, experience and exam records move with you and support re-certification by your next employer.

What is the difference between Level II and Level III?

A Level II performs, interprets and reports examinations. A Level III establishes and approves procedures, interprets codes, and trains and examines Level I and II personnel. See ASNT Level III training.

Can I practise before my practical exam?

Yes. The Practical NDT simulator offers 12 methods in five environments, including an oil and gas site and a storage tank. It is practice only and does not replace hands-on training or the practical exam.

Where can I read about NDT pay in the Houston area?

We don't publish local salary figures. Our NDT salary guide explains how level, method and sector drive pay.
